archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since my sophomore year, which has been an eye-opening experience. It's given me insights into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I initially didn't see myself going down the research route, but a professor noticed my skills in bridging technical coding with user experience and suggested I apply for a research assistant position in a data visualization lab. I was hesitant at first, but it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.research_experience_short: I've been involved in undergrad research since my sophomore year. It's been an eye-opening experience, giving me insights into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I initially didn't see myself going down the research route, but a professor noticed my skills in bridging technical coding with user experience and suggested I apply for a research assistant position in a data visualization lab. It turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.research_lab: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. We deal with datasets that are tens of terabytes in size. My main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.first_research_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. The raw data consisted of daily temperature readings from buoys across the Pacific, which was enormous and scattered across different servers. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to zoom into specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored my first paper on this system, which was a surreal and proud moment in college.
archival_memory.current_research: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can enhance scientists' understanding of complex data. By providing an interactive 3D environment, researchers can manipulate and analyze data in a more intuitive way. It's a leap from traditional coding and data visualization, requiring experimentation with VR headsets, integration with engines like Unity or Unreal, and efficient data streaming. The cutting-edge nature of this field makes it exciting, as I'm forging my own path and contributing to the development of VR data visualization.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding; it's also about reading and staying up-to-date with the latest advancements in the field. I spend a significant amount of time reading academic papers, conference proceedings, and workshops to find solutions to specific problems. It can be overwhelming, but I've learned to skim through papers effectively by focusing on the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Sharing interesting discoveries with the lab and discussing how to incorporate new techniques into our workflow is a great way to collaborate and improve our research.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep knowledge in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their dedication and creativity. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets and integrating it with our VR platform. This allows for real-time performance improvements by only loading a compressed representation of the data until zooming in. Working alongside him and other students provides valuable insights into how theoretical concepts are applied in practice. Spontaneous brainstorming sessions, like in the lab break room, often lead to innovative ideas and solutions.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research through poster presentations at smaller symposiums around campus. It's a great experience that requires distilling complex research into easy-to-understand visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about presenting, but it turned out to be a friendly dialogue with genuine interest from attendees. Even industry professionals and local startup representatives shared valuable insights on how VR for data visualization could be applied in commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. These interactions opened my eyes to the potential real-world applications of our research.
archival_memory.publications: I've been fortunate enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission for the IEEE Visualization Conference. Our research focuses on comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment in a user study. We hypothesize that VR immersion helps researchers spot anomalies or trends faster. We conducted a small user trial with 15 participants, recorded their times, and gathered UX feedback. Now, we're analyzing the data to determine if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a collaborative effort, with each of us contributing our expertise. It's a balancing act, especially with senior coursework and a capstone project to manage.
archival_memory.future_plans: I'm considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. I want to contribute to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning, but I also want to see how these concepts are applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that stepping into industry can provide a better understanding of relevant problems, which would be beneficial if I decide to return for a PhD with a more practical approach.
archival_memory.research_challenges: Research can be frustrating, with weeks spent on approaches that don't pan out or discovering that existing ideas have been improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate new findings into our work. By reading existing papers, thinking of new angles or applications, and pushing boundaries, we can contribute to the ever-growing foundation of knowledge. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special, as we build upon the work of others and strive for innovation.
archival_memory.server_crash: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, causing a scramble to recover vital data. Although we managed to restore most of it, the crisis highlighted the importance of data backups. We learned from the experience and set up a better backup system to prevent similar incidents in the future. It was a stressful event, but it also brought the lab together and taught us valuable lessons.
archival_memory.research_connections: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student. My PI is very approachable and supportive, offering guidance on career direction and helping me with scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I've had the chance to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met experts from around the world debating technical details and proposing new frameworks. Witnessing the frontier of CS knowledge in real time was truly fascinating. These connections have enriched my research experience and opened doors to new opportunities.
archival_memory.research_journey: My journey in the research world has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that my work in the lab could shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're pioneering might one day become standard tools, and I'd be proud to have been part of that from the beginning. The sense of contributing to something bigger keeps me motivated. This experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the perspectives I've gained. I couldn't imagine my undergrad years without this experience—it's enriched my understanding of what it means to be a computer scientist.
